claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The intervention is substitution of Hf with Ti.
Replacing a heavier constituent with a lighter constituent can reduce RHEA density.
Replacing Hf with Ti in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr will reduce density without sacrificing room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
The proposed performance boundary spans room temperature to 1600 °C.
Yield strength and fracture toughness are the specified mechanical loading responses.
A BCC crystal structure is the structural mediator in the modified HfMoTaTiZr alloy.
The intervention will produce or retain a solid solution through alloying and phase stability.
The modified alloy may form a BCC+B2 microstructure.
The modified alloy will have a density 5–10% lower than the as-cast baseline.
The modified alloy will retain a room-temperature yield strength above 1500 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain a yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline density is 10.21 g cm−3.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline room-temperature yield strength is 1600 MPa.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline yield strength at 1000 °C is 855 MPa.
The controlled evaluation will use compression tests at room temperature and 1000 °C together with density measurements.
The experiment will measure yield strength, fracture toughness, and density.
A density reduction below 3% falsifies the hypothesis.
A yield-strength decrease greater than 10% at room temperature or 1000 °C falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires a 5–10% density reduction, but the hypothesis is rejected only below 3%, leaving reductions from 3% to under 5% inconsistent with the prediction yet non-falsifying.

A room-temperature strength loss of up to 10% is allowed by the rejection rule; from the stated 1600 MPa baseline this permits values as low as 1440 MPa, contradicting the predicted threshold above 1500 MPa.

Fracture toughness is specified as a response and measurement, but the design only identifies compression testing and gives no fracture-toughness test or rejection threshold. The design also stops at 1000 °C despite a stated boundary extending to 1600 °C.
